scanner.title: OBD2 Scanner
scanner.unsupportedTitle: Bluetooth is not available in this browser
scanner.unsupportedBody: The live scanner needs Web Bluetooth: use Chrome or Edge on Android, Windows, macOS or ChromeOS. Safari and iPhone/iPad are not supported.
scanner.howTo: Plug a Bluetooth LE ELM327 adapter (e.g. Vgate iCar Pro BLE, OBDLink CX, Veepeak BLE+) into the OBD2 port, turn the ignition on, then connect. Classic-Bluetooth and Wi-Fi adapters cannot be used from a browser.
scanner.noPids: The car didn't report any reading this app understands.
scanner.recordHint: Record a drive to save it as a session — it gets the same charts, flags and AI analysis as an uploaded CSV.
scanner.selectCar: Select a vehicle in the sidebar to save this recording.
scanner.clearDtcs: Clear the codes in the car
scanner.clearTitle: Clear the codes in the car?
scanner.clearBody: This turns off the check-engine light and erases stored codes, freeze-frame data and readiness monitors. The fault itself is not fixed and the code will come back if it persists. Do this with the engine off and the ignition on.
scanner.linkHintBusy: The adapter accepts one connection at a time. Disconnect it from other apps or devices before connecting in Xpeed.
scanner.linkHintPower: Make sure the ignition is on and the adapter light is on, then unplug and replug it to wake it up.
scanner.linkHintPaired: Bluetooth LE: keep Bluetooth on and select the adapter directly in Xpeed; no pairing in Android settings is needed. In the Android APK, Classic Bluetooth requires pairing in Android settings first, then selection in Xpeed.

custom.title: Custom PIDs
custom.hint: Manufacturer-specific data (e.g. Toyota hybrid ECU on header 7E2/7E3, mode 21). In formulas, A, B, C… are the reply bytes, e.g. (A*256+B)/10. Compare the values with the dashboard before trusting them.
custom.needsCan: This vehicle is not CAN, so PIDs with an ECU header cannot be read.
custom.name: Name

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.hint: Send a read request to a car module and see the raw answer — useful to find manufacturer data. Read-only: nothing is changed in the car.

scan.title: ECU discovery
scan.copied: Copied — paste it in the chat
scan.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard
scan.hint: Find which modules answer and list every mode 21 data block of each one. Run it twice (e.g. engine off and on) to highlight the bytes that change — those are live sensors. Read-only: nothing is changed in the car; live data pauses during the sweep.

scanner.codesHint: Asks every module in the car which fault codes it has stored. Reading changes nothing in the car. What it finds also goes to Problems in the app.
scanner.dangerTitle: Clear the codes in the car
scanner.dangerBody: Erases the codes from the car's memory and turns off the check-engine light on the dashboard. It doesn't fix anything: if the fault is still there, the car stores the code again and the light comes back on. That's also how you check whether a problem is really gone.
scanner.codesLegend: Pending: the car saw it once and is still confirming. Permanent: only the car itself erases it, after confirming the fault is gone.
scanner.clearInCar: In the car: the fault codes, the check-engine light, the snapshot of when the fault happened (freeze frame) and the readiness tests are erased.
scanner.clearNotFixed: Nothing is repaired: if the fault is still there, the car stores the code and turns the light on again when it tests that system — this can take a few days of driving.
scanner.clearInspection: Until the car finishes its tests, it can fail a vehicle inspection.
scanner.clearInApp: In the app: these problems are marked as solved; if a code comes back, the problem reappears as "came back".
scanner.clearHow: Do it with the engine off and the ignition on.
scanner.clearList: Codes that will be erased in the car: {{codes}}
scanner.clearReadFirst: Read the car's codes first to see what will be erased.
scanner.clearPermanent: Permanent codes ({{codes}}) are not erased: the car erases them itself once it confirms the fault is gone.
scanner.clearedHint: The check-engine light should go off. If the fault is still there, the car turns it on again after testing.

generic.meaning: A reading was outside its normal range during a trip.
generic.action: Keep an eye on it; if it keeps happening, mention it at your next service.

dtc.meaning: The car's computer recorded a fault in the {{area}}.

action.severe: See a mechanic as soon as possible and show them this code.
action.moderate: Book a check-up and show the mechanic this code.
action.minor: It can wait for your next service; mention this code.

dtc.pendingMeaning: The car's computer noticed a possible fault in the {{area}} once and is checking whether it happens again.
dtc.pendingAction: No need to rush. If the car confirms it, it shows here as a fault code with what to do; if not, it goes away by itself.

coolant_temp.title: Engine running hot
coolant_temp.meaning: The engine temperature stayed above normal for a while.
coolant_temp.action: Check the coolant level with the engine cold. If the temperature gauge climbs again, pull over safely and see a mechanic.

engine_rpm.title: Engine revving very high
engine_rpm.meaning: The engine spun close to its limit for a long time.
engine_rpm.action: Avoid revving hard, especially with a cold engine or in a low gear. If it wasn't you, have it checked.

battery_voltage_12v.title: Weak 12 V battery
battery_voltage_12v.meaning: The small 12 V battery's voltage went outside the normal range.
battery_voltage_12v.action: Ask for a battery and charging-system test at your next service, or sooner if the car is slow to start.

intake_air_temp.title: Hot air going into the engine
intake_air_temp.meaning: The air the engine breathes was hotter than normal.
intake_air_temp.action: Check the air filter and that nothing blocks the air intake.

fuel_trim.title: Fuel mixture out of balance
fuel_trim.meaning: The engine is correcting its air–fuel mix more than usual.
fuel_trim.action: Often an air leak, a dirty sensor or injectors. Book a check-up; it's not urgent if the car drives fine.

engine_load.title: Engine working very hard
engine_load.meaning: The engine ran near full effort for a long time.
engine_load.action: Normal on steep hills or with a heavy load. If it happens on regular drives, have it checked.

oil_temp.title: Engine oil running hot
oil_temp.meaning: The engine oil got hotter than normal.
oil_temp.action: Check the oil level and when it was last changed.

transmission_temp.title: Gearbox running hot
transmission_temp.meaning: The transmission fluid got hotter than normal.
transmission_temp.action: Avoid towing or heavy loads and have the transmission fluid checked.

motor_temp.title: Electric motor running hot
motor_temp.meaning: An electric drive motor got hotter than normal.
motor_temp.action: Drive gently and have the cooling system checked by a specialist.

hv_battery.title: Hybrid battery outside its normal range
hv_battery.meaning: The high-voltage battery's charge or voltage went outside the usual range.
hv_battery.action: If it keeps happening, have the hybrid battery checked by a hybrid specialist.

hv_battery_temp.title: Hybrid battery running hot
hv_battery_temp.meaning: The high-voltage battery got hotter than normal.
hv_battery_temp.action: Check that the battery cooling vent (usually near the rear seat) is not blocked or dirty.

inverter_temp.title: Hybrid system running hot
inverter_temp.meaning: The hybrid system's inverter got hotter than normal.
inverter_temp.action: Check the inverter coolant level and have the hybrid cooling pump checked.

catalyst_temp.title: Catalytic converter very hot
catalyst_temp.meaning: The exhaust catalytic converter got hotter than normal.
catalyst_temp.action: This can come from misfires or a rich mixture. Book a check-up.

companionSite.title: Xpeed Companion
companionSite.intro: Xpeed Companion is a small Windows app that reads the telemetry of your racing game while you drive. Every lap goes to your Xpeed account, where you can see it, compare it and get faster.
companionSite.checksumHelp: SHA-256 of the installer. In PowerShell, Get-FileHash on the downloaded file must give the same value.
companionSite.smartscreen: If Windows warns about an unknown publisher: click More info, then Run anyway. The checksum above lets you verify that the file is the one we published.
companionSite.step1Text: Run the installer. Xpeed Companion starts with Windows and stays in the tray, next to the clock.
companionSite.step2Text: Click Connect to your account. Your browser opens on Xpeed and asks you once to confirm. The page shows a 4-letter verification code: check that it is the same one shown in the app, then confirm.
companionSite.step3Text: Start your game and drive. Each lap arrives in the Virtual area of your Xpeed account, with its track map, speed and pedals.
companionSite.certifiedText: Tested with the real game: laps, track map and inputs are checked.
companionSite.betaText: Supported, but still being checked with the real game. Some data may be missing.
companionSite.faqSentA: Your laps (lap time, car, track and the readings of each lap), the track layouts, and the name of your computer so you can recognise it in your account. Nothing else is read from your PC.
companionSite.faqDisconnectA: In Xpeed, open Virtual > Xpeed Companion and click Revoke next to the computer. It can no longer send laps; laps already sent stay in your account. To pause recording, use the icon in the tray.
companionSite.faqFilesA: Laps are saved in Documents\Xpeed Companion\Laps. Settings and the log are in %APPDATA%\Xpeed Companion. The key that connects your PC to your account is protected by Windows and never shown.
companionSite.faqRemoveA: Windows Settings > Apps > Installed apps > Xpeed Companion > Uninstall. Then revoke the computer in your account. Your lap files in Documents are not deleted.
companionSite.privacy: Privacy: Xpeed Companion reads only the telemetry your racing game publishes and sends laps only to your own Xpeed account, over HTTPS.

landing.tagline: Know if your car is OK, in plain words.
landing.signInTitle: Sign in or create your account
landing.signInHint: With your phone number: we text you a code. No password.
landing.useEmail: I have an account with email and password
landing.title: Know if your car is OK, without knowing mechanics.
landing.subtitle: A pocket adapter reads your car, Xpeed records every trip on its own and tells you in plain words what needs attention.
landing.point1: Works with most cars from 2008 on
landing.point2: Android phone or Chrome on a computer
landing.f1Text: Leave the app open in the car. Every trip is recorded and checked, with nothing to tap.
landing.f2Text: If something is off, you see what it means and what to do: wait, book a check-up or stop now.
landing.f3Text: Send a link with the fault codes and readings, so the mechanic starts from facts.
landing.s1: Get an OBD2 adapter with "Bluetooth LE" in the name (for example Veepeak OBDCheck BLE).
landing.s2: Plug it in under the steering wheel and turn the car on.
landing.s3: Sign in with your phone, tap "Connect to the car" and pick the adapter. From then on Xpeed does the rest.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This text explains in plain words which data Xpeed keeps, what for, who else receives it and how you control all of it. It covers the website, the Android app and Xpeed Companion.

who.title: Who is responsible
p: The controller of your data is the Xpeed service ("Xpeed", "we"). How to reach us is in the Contact section at the end of this page.

data.title: Which data we keep
p: We keep data in two groups, depending on what you use.
items: Real car: your account (the phone number or the Google account e-mail you sign in with), your cars, trips and their readings, fault codes, fuel and maintenance records and the photos you add yourself.

Racing games (Virtual): the lap telemetry sent by Xpeed Companion (speed, pedals, steering, position on the track, fuel, tyre and brake data and session details such as the weather), the game, track and car names, lap and sector times, your computer's name and the date it was last seen, a profile with a handle and display name, friends, shared links and reports.

companion.title: What Xpeed Companion sends (and never sends)
p: Xpeed Companion is the Windows program that reads your game.
items: It sends: laps and track layouts built from the game's own files, the computer name and the account label.
It never sends: your Windows user name, files outside Companion's own folder, data of other programs, or the device key in diagnostics.
The key that links the computer to your account is kept protected by Windows.

profile.title: Public profile and shared links
p: Your profile is public by default. In the profile settings you can choose public, friends only or private at any time.

A public profile shows your display name, handle, best laps and rankings. Your e-mail, phone number and account name are never shown. If you do not pick a name, we generate a default one to show instead.
A share link shows the lap to anyone who has the link, until you revoke it or it expires.

why.title: Why we use it and on what basis
p: We use the data to provide the service (record trips and laps, show analysis), to build rankings and to keep things secure. In plain words, the legal basis is:
items: your consent, when you sign up and connect Companion (you can withdraw it at any time);
performance of the service you asked for;
legitimate interest, for security and to prevent abuse and fraud.

where.title: Where and for how long
p: The data is stored on Xpeed's own server and connections use HTTPS. We keep it until you delete the data or the account.
Laps older than 90 days that are not a personal best and are not marked are kept in a reduced version, with 10 samples per second. Times and summaries stay complete.

rights.title: Your rights (LGPD and GDPR)
p: Under the LGPD, and in the same words under the GDPR, you can ask for:
items: access and a copy of your data;
correction of wrong data;
deletion of your data;
portability, which means taking your data with you;
objection to a use of your data;
withdrawal of consent, at any time.
after: To use them: use the export and delete options on the privacy settings page, or contact us as described below. To stop sending laps, revoke the computer in your account. If you think we handle your data wrongly, you can complain to the data protection authority of your country.

third.title: Third parties
p: We do not sell data and we show no advertising. We use no analytics tools or third-party trackers: we only keep your language and your sign-in session on your device. These companies receive data in specific cases:
items: Sign-in: Google (Firebase) confirms your number by text message or your Google account. Google reCAPTCHA is also used for phone sign-in in the browser.
Fonts: the pages load fonts from Google Fonts, so Google receives your IP address when a page opens.

AI, Real car only: the AI provider (OpenRouter and the model chosen) receives data only when the feature acts: when a trip worth a summary is saved (car details, duration, fault codes and summarised readings), in questions to the assistant (with the car's open problems, recent trips and maintenance) and when a fuel receipt photo is read. Nothing from racing games goes to the AI.
VIN: if you type a VIN to fill in the car's details, it is looked up in the public NHTSA vPIC decoder, in the USA.
GitHub: the download of Companion and of the Android app is a GitHub link, and the Android app checks there for a new version. GitHub sees the request (for example your IP address).

children.title: Children
p: Xpeed is not meant for people under 13 (or under the minimum age in the law of your country, if higher). If we learn of such an account, we will delete it.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
p: We may update this text. The "Last updated" date at the top shows the version in force. For important changes, we will tell you in the app.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.intro: By creating an account or using Xpeed you agree to these terms. They are short on purpose.

service.title: What Xpeed is
p: Xpeed has two parts: Real car, which reads your car through an OBD2 adapter and explains in plain words what needs attention, and Virtual, which receives through Xpeed Companion the laps from your racing games so you can analyse them, compare them and climb the rankings.
It is a hobby project, provided as is.

account.title: Your account
p: You sign in with your phone or your Google account. Look after access to your device and your account: whatever is done through it is your responsibility. Give true information and do not create new accounts to get around a suspension.

content.title: Names and public content
p: Handles, display names and any public text follow these rules:
items: nothing offensive or discriminatory;
nothing that impersonates another person, team or brand;
nothing you have no right to publish.

fair.title: Fair play
p: Do not fake laps, telemetry or times, and do not use the service to cheat the rankings. Laps are checked, and those that look impossible are left out of the rankings. Do not try to reach other people's data or to overload or attack the service either.
Xpeed may hide content and suspend accounts for abuse.

data.title: Your data
p: Your data stays yours. By using Xpeed you give the service the right to store it and to show it as you chose (for example a public profile, friends or shared links), only so that the service works. The details are in the Privacy Policy.

warranty.title: No warranty
p: Xpeed does not promise that it will work without errors or interruptions.
In Real car it gives hints from data, not a diagnosis: with warning lights or serious symptoms, see a mechanic.

liability.title: Limits of liability
p: As far as the law allows, Xpeed is not liable for indirect damages, lost profits, lost data or decisions made from the app's hints, such as maintenance or driving. Use it at your own risk and never in a way that takes your attention off the road or the track. Nothing here limits rights that the law does not allow to be limited.

companion.title: Xpeed Companion
p: Xpeed Companion is software provided as is. It updates itself (it checks for new versions in the background and installs them, never during a game). You can turn automatic updates off in Companion itself.

ending.title: Ending an account
p: You can delete your account whenever you like on the privacy settings page; that deletes your data. We may suspend or close accounts that break these terms, and the service may change or end.

changes.title: Changes to the terms
p: We may update these terms. The "Last updated" date at the top shows the version in force. Continuing to use Xpeed after a change means you accept it.

law.title: Applicable law
p: These terms follow the law of the country where the service operator is established.
